sources.note: Bibliography only. Besides Muti 2013 and Setyaningsih 2014 the Onin entries are 19th-20th c. ethnography/wordlists (Modera 1830 numerals; Earl 1853; Müller 1857; Robidé van der Aa 1879; de Clercq 1889/1893; Galis 1955), Walker 1978 Bomberai survey report (unpublished), Smits & Voorhoeve 1992 Anceaux wordlists, Donohue 1996 on Onin Pidgin, Kaplan 2026. No grammar or grammar sketch of Onin exists in Glottolog.

sources.citation: Kaplan, Johanna. 2026. Supplemental material for 'Bomberai Tip as a language chain: A lexical similarity analysis of the relationship between Onin, Sekar and Uruangnirin' (BA thesis, Uppsala University). Zenodo dataset, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18507877; Onin sheet transcribed from Eline Visser's 2025 PARADISEC Onin wordlist EV2-words_syntax (consultant Samsulando Garamatan)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose statement. The 463-item Onin wordlist carries apostrophe stress marks before the stressed syllable ('pati 'stone', i'gai 'sand', ka'bisak, sa'nanan, wara'beta). My own tally of single-word forms (not a source claim): disyllables 130 penult vs 52 final (20 unmarked); trisyllables 118 penult vs 10 final vs 1 initial (10 unmarked); 4-syllable 15 penult, 1 final, 1 antepenult. Many final-stressed forms end in a diphthong or closed syllable (i'gai, ma'rop, ka'nus, me'sia), so the pattern looks penultimate-default with a final-stress minority, but no published rule exists.

sources.note: Nothing: a pronoun-morphology article (personal, demonstrative, interrogative pronouns); the only phonological remark is that most pronouns are di- or trisyllabic (p. 290); no tekanan/aksen/stress anywhere. Useful for identity: Onin has 4 dialects (Nikuda, Patipi, Ogar, Sepa); BP2B 2013 lumps Sekar and Onim as one language 'Sekar-Onim' with 78.75% lexical difference between the two dialects (p. 286).
